title: Terms and Conditions (Complete Recording)
description: A tuxedoed crooner sings a licensing agreement in full. The tempo climbs 2 BPM per section because the trial is expiring; it stops mid-word on a chime.
stylePrompt:
Vegas big-band showstopper, 124 BPM at the top, performing an end-user license
agreement in full. Full horn section, walking upright bass, ride cymbal, a
string sweep on every subheading. Deadpan baritone crooner in a tuxedo who
believes this is the best material he has ever been given — warm, generous,
selling it to the back row. Never winking; the sincerity is the entire act.
**Structural flaw:** the tempo increases 2 BPM at every section break because
the free trial is expiring, and nobody in the band acknowledges it. By the
arbitration clause the band is at 138; by the final section it is at 152 and
the words are no longer fully intelligible. The song does not end — it stops
mid-word on a sampled interface chime. Horn stabs on all-caps clauses only.
Optional tiny audience applause bed that never grows. Runtime ~1:50–2:15. Use
a deadpan baritone or Continuity Voice with a bigger room; do not use Rubella.
lyrics:
[Overture — 8 bars, 124 BPM]
(horns, string sweep, one ride crash)

[Verse 1 — Acceptance]
By clicking, tapping, breathing near this screen
By continuing to exist inside this room
You accept the terms as written
And the terms as they will be
And the terms we haven't finished yet
(that last one's my favorite)

[Chorus 1]
Terms! And! Conditions!
Read in full for the very first time
Somebody finally sang them, folks
Somebody finally gave them a rhyme
Nothing in this agreement is a promise
Nothing in this agreement is a lie
Terms and conditions apply

[Verse 2 — Section 4: Limitation of Liability — 126 BPM]
We are not liable for the hallway
We are not liable for the light
We are not liable for anything that happened
Between the hours of any night
Not liable for the elevator's opinions
Not liable for the sky above the lot
Our maximum liability, in aggregate, forever
Is the amount you have already forgot

[Chorus 2 — 128 BPM]
Terms! And! Conditions!
Section four, subsection C
You waived it in a hallway in November
You waived it on behalf of me
You waived it for your heirs and your assignees
And the version of yourself you'll be
Terms and conditions apply

[Section 9 — Arbitration — 138 BPM, key change up a whole step]
Any dispute! Any claim! Any grievance or complaint!
Shall be resolved in a room that we describe as a room
By a neutral third party that we personally selected
And who is, at this time, unavailable
YOU HAVE WAIVED YOUR RIGHT TO A JURY
YOU HAVE WAIVED YOUR RIGHT TO A CLASS
You may opt out within thirty days
Of a date we have not published yet
(horn stab)

[Section 12 — Changes to These Terms — 146 BPM, breathless]
We may amend, we may revise, we may replace, we may rescind
Continued use constitutes acceptance
Continued life constitutes continued use
We will notify you by a method
We will notify you eventually
We will notify you by the sound of this song

[Final Section — 152 BPM, unintelligible, joyful]
Severability governing-law entire-agreement force-majeure
No-waiver no-warranty as-is as-available where-is
Survives termination survives assignment survives you
Survives the building survives the channel survives the
(interface chime)

[Outro]
(silence)
(single string sweep, unresolved)
notes:
## What the song is
A tuxedo crooner performs a licensing agreement end to end as if it were the
great American songbook standard nobody has had the courage to attempt. He is
not mocking the document. He thinks it is beautiful. The audience bed never
grows, and he never notices that either.

The gag is legal-adjacent set dressing only — invented clauses for a fake
low-power affiliate, not advice, not a real agreement, not a parody of any
specific company's terms.
